title: SUID literature from the Ramirez lab and Lavista Ferres group: abstracts (PubMed, retrieved 2026-10-26)
research_questions: To determine whether maternal obesity is a risk factor for Sudden Unexpected Infant Death (SUID) and the proportion of SUID cases attributable to maternal obesity.
To examine pandemic-era changes in non-SUID infant mortality by gestational age, age at death and cause of death.
To investigate the effects of maternal prepregnancy smoking, reduction during pregnancy, and smoking during pregnancy on SUID rates.
To assess whether inner ear dysfunction not only weakens the hypercapnic response, but also plays a role in suppressing the arousal response to suffocating gas mixtures.
To investigate the role of PiCo and preBötC in respiratory-sympathetic coupling under control conditions and following exposure to chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH).
To report results from an 11-step user-centered design development process for a quit smoking conversational chatbot called QuitBot.
To investigate whether mouse models of Leigh Syndrome exhibit dysfunctions in neuromuscular activity of swallow and breathing integration.
How does chronic intermittent hypoxia (IH) affect adult neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus?
What are the effects of IH on synaptic plasticity in the dentate gyrus?
Do reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent and ROS-independent mechanisms contribute to changes in adult neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity due to IH?
How do breathing patterns during the first hour after birth predict survival in mice born prematurely or at term?
What are the roles of inhibition within the pre-Bötzinger complex (preBötC) for rhythm generation?
Does chronic intermittent hypoxia differentially impact inspiratory activity states at the level of the preBötzinger Complex?
Can progesterone pretreatment ameliorate detrimental effects of lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation on cortical neurogenesis in mice?

claims.quote: Taken together, these results suggest that PiCo and preBötC contribute to respiratory-sympathetic coupling, which is altered by CIH, and may contribute to the hypertension observed in patients with OSA.

claims.quote: We hypothesized that breathing patterns during the first hour of life would be predictive of survival in an animal model of prematurity.

claims.quote: Overall, mice that survived had higher birth weights and showed eupneic or gasping activity that was able to transition to normal breathing.

claims.statement: Mice that did not survive exhibited distinct large amplitude breaths at low frequency, failing to transition into normal breathing.
claims.quote: In contrast, mice that did not survive showed distinct, large amplitude, long-lasting breaths that occurred at low frequency and did not transition into eupnea.

claims.statement: Local inhibition destabilizes rhythmogenesis while long-range inhibition stabilizes it in the pre-Bötzinger complex inspiratory microcircuit.
claims.quote: Increasing inhibition within the microcircuit results in a limited number of out-of-phase neurons before rhythmicity and synchrony degenerate. Thus unstructured local inhibition is destabilizing and cannot support the generation of more than one rhythm.

claims.statement: The study used a biophysical model to investigate the roles of local and long-range inhibition in the respiratory network, supported by in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
claims.quote: We use a biophysical model to investigate the different roles of local and long-range inhibition in the respiratory network, a key component of which is the pre-Bötzinger complex inspiratory microcircuit.

claims.statement: Partial excitation block leads to increased rhythmic variability but recovers after blockade of inhibition in the pre-Bötzinger complex.
claims.quote: Partial excitation block leads to increased rhythmic variability, but this recovers after blockade of inhibition.

claims.statement: Chronic intermittent hypoxia differentially impacts inspiratory activity states at the level of the pre-Bötzinger complex.
claims.quote: The preBötzinger complex (preBötC) is a medullary brainstem network crucially involved in the generation of different inspiratory rhythms. In the isolated brainstem slice, the preBötC reconfigures to produce different rhythms that we refer to as 'fictive eupnea' under baseline conditions (i.e., carbogen), and 'fictive gasping' in hypoxia.

claims.statement: The study examined the impact of chronic intermittent hypoxia on various dynamic aspects of rhythmogenesis during baseline conditions, transition to hypoxia, and throughout hypoxia.
claims.quote: We recently demonstrated that fictive eupnea is irregular following exposure to chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH). However, it is unknown how CIH impacts fictive gasping. To address this, brain slices containing the preBötC were prepared from control and CIH exposed mice. Electrophysiological recordings of rhythmogenesis were obtained during the perihypoxic interval.

claims.statement: Chronic intermittent hypoxia increased irregularity score (IrS) and fluctuation value (χ) but did not affect sample entropy (sENT) of amplitude in baseline conditions.
claims.quote: In baseline conditions, CIH increased IrS of amplitude (0.21 ± 0.2) and χ of amplitude (0.34 ± 0.02) but did not affect sENT of amplitude.

claims.statement: During hypoxia, all slices from CIH-exposed mice exhibited rhythms throughout the interval, while only a fraction of control rhythms maintained rhythmicity.
claims.quote: While 29% of control rhythms maintained rhythmicity throughout hypoxia, all slices from CIH exposed mice exhibited rhythms throughout the hypoxic interval.

claims.statement: Progesterone pretreatment ameliorates detrimental effects of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammation on cortical neurogenesis in mice.
claims.quote: Our objective was to determine if progesterone pretreatment could ameliorate the detrimental effects of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammation on cortical neurogenesis.

claims.statement: The study used two-color immunofluorescence with primary antibodies to assess Tbr2 intermediate neural progenitor cell density, microglia activation, and cell death rates after LPS exposure.
claims.quote: Two-color immunofluorescence was performed with primary antibodies T-box transcription factor 2 (Tbr2), ionized calcium binding adapter molecule 1 (Iba1), cleaved caspase 3 (CC3), and 5-bromo-2'-deoxyuridine (BrdU). Cells were counted, and statistical analysis was determined using analysis of variance and Tukey-Kramer method.

claims.statement: Lipopolysaccharide exposure reduced Tbr2 intermediate neural progenitor cell density but increased microglia activation and cell death rates.
claims.quote: The Tbr2 intermediate neural progenitor cell density decreased after LPS exposure (P = .0022). After LPS exposure, microglia displayed an activated phenotype, and cell density was increased (P < .001). Cell death rates were low among study groups but was increased in LPS exposure groups compared to progesterone alone (P = .0015).

claims.statement: Pre-exposure with progesterone statistically increased Tbr2 intermediate neural progenitors and protected against cell death induced by LPS.
claims.quote: Pre-exposure to progesterone statistically increased Tbr2 intermediate neural progenitors compared to LPS treatment alone and was similar to controls (P = .0022). After LPS exposure, microglia displayed an activated phenotype, and cell density was increased (P < .001). Cell death rates were low among study groups but was increased in LPS exposure groups compared to progesterone alone (P = .0015).

claims.statement: Chronic intermittent hypoxia alters local respiratory circuit function at the level of the pre-Bötzinger complex.
claims.quote: The preBötzinger complex (preBötC) is a pre-motor respiratory network critical for inspiratory rhythm generation. Here, we test the hypothesis that CIH increases irregular output from the isolated preBötC, which can be mitigated by antioxidant treatment.

claims.statement: The study used electrophysiological recordings to examine burst-to-burst irregularity in period and amplitude of rhythmogenesis following chronic intermittent hypoxia exposure.
claims.quote: Electrophysiological recordings from brainstem slices revealed that CIH enhanced burst-to-burst irregularity in period and/or amplitude.

claims.statement: Chronic intermittent hypoxia increased lipid peroxidation in the pre-Bötzinger complex, which was reduced by antioxidant treatment.
claims.quote: CIH increased the degree of lipid peroxidation in the preBötC and treatment with the antioxidant, 5,10,15,20-Tetrakis (1-methylpyridinium-4-yl)-21H,23H-porphyrin manganese(III) pentachloride (MnTMPyP), reduced CIH-mediated irregularities on the network rhythm and improved transmission of preBötC to the XIIn.

claims.statement: Excessive sensory stimulation during development alters neural plasticity and vulnerability to cocaine in mice.
claims.quote: Early life experiences affect the formation of neuronal networks, which can have a profound impact on brain function and behavior later in life. Previous work has shown that mice exposed to excessive sensory stimulation during development are hyperactive and novelty seeking, and display impaired cognition compared with controls.

claims.statement: The study assessed the reinforcing properties of cocaine and underlying circuitry in CD-1 mice exposed to excessive sensory stimulation during development.
claims.quote: In this study, we addressed the issue of whether excessive sensory stimulation during development could alter behaviors related to addiction and underlying circuitry in CD-1 mice.

claims.statement: Mice exposed to excessive sensory stimulation showed enhanced reinforcing properties of cocaine but impaired persistence of cocaine-induced locomotor sensitization.
claims.quote: We found that the reinforcing properties of cocaine were significantly enhanced in mice exposed to excessive sensory stimulation. Moreover, although these mice displayed hyperactivity that became more pronounced over time, they showed impaired persistence of cocaine-induced locomotor sensitization.

claims.statement: Excessive sensory stimulation altered glutamatergic transmission in the nucleus accumbens and amygdala, affecting behaviors related to addiction.
claims.quote: These behavioral effects were associated with alterations in glutamatergic transmission in the nucleus accumbens and amygdala.

claims.statement: Microcircuits in respiratory rhythm generation share commonalities with other rhythm generating networks, including synaptic inhibition and excitation roles.
claims.quote: Rhythmicity is critical for the generation of rhythmic behaviors and higher brain functions. This review discusses common mechanisms of rhythm generation, including the role of synaptic inhibition and excitation, with a focus on the mammalian respiratory network.
